subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: On the INSIDE of a meander bend, where the water is slower, the river usually:
options: Deposits sediment forming a slip-off slope (point bar)
questions.explain: Slower flow on the inner bend deposits sediment, building a gently sloping point bar.

questions.q: On a flood hydrograph, the 'lag time' is the gap between:
questions.explain: Lag time is the delay between the heaviest rainfall and the river reaching its highest discharge.

questions.q: Dissolved minerals carried invisibly in the water are transported by:
questions.explain: In solution, dissolved load is carried chemically within the water.

questions.q: Why does deforestation in a drainage basin increase flood risk?
options: Less interception and infiltration means water reaches the river faster
questions.explain: Removing trees cuts interception and infiltration, so rain runs quickly into the river, raising flood risk.

questions.q: A delta forms where a river:
options: Deposits its load as it enters a sea or lake
Begins at its source on a mountain
questions.explain: Deltas form where a river deposits sediment as it slows on entering still water.

questions.q: The water that flows over the surface into a river without soaking in is called:
questions.explain: Surface run-off (overland flow) is water moving across the ground straight into the river.

questions.q: The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries is the:
questions.explain: A drainage basin is the whole area of land drained by a river system.

questions.q: Transport in which small particles bounce along the river bed is called:
questions.explain: Saltation is the bouncing or hopping of small particles along the bed.

questions.q: A river generally has its greatest discharge and carries its largest total load in its:
questions.explain: By the lower course, tributaries have added water, so discharge and total load are greatest.

questions.q: The process by which water turns from liquid into vapour and rises into the atmosphere is:
questions.explain: Evaporation turns liquid water into water vapour that rises into the air.

questions.q: The boundary separating one drainage basin from another is the:
questions.explain: The watershed is the ridge of high land marking the edge of a drainage basin.

questions.q: Erosion caused by the sheer force of fast-moving water hitting and pushing into cracks in the bank is called:
questions.explain: Hydraulic action is the force of water compressing air in cracks, weakening rock.

questions.q: Which is a HUMAN cause of increased river flooding?
options: Building on floodplains and creating impermeable surfaces
questions.explain: Urbanisation adds impermeable surfaces and drains, speeding water into rivers.

questions.q: The point where a tributary joins the main river is called the:
questions.explain: A confluence is the point where a tributary meets the main river channel.

questions.q: Which is an example of SOFT engineering flood management?
questions.explain: Soft engineering, like planting trees and zoning land use, works with natural processes.

questions.q: Which is an example of HARD engineering river flood management?
options: Building a concrete dam and reservoir
Allowing the river to flood washland
questions.explain: Dams and reservoirs are hard engineering structures that control river flow.

questions.q: When rocks knock together and become smaller and rounder, the process is:
questions.explain: Attrition wears rocks down as they collide, making them smaller and rounder.

questions.q: The flat area either side of a river that floods and is built up by deposited sediment is the:
questions.explain: A floodplain is the wide, flat valley floor built up by sediment left behind when the river floods.

questions.q: A waterfall and its plunge pool are typically formed where the river crosses:
options: A band of hard rock over softer rock
A band of soft rock over hard rock
questions.explain: Soft rock beneath a hard cap is eroded faster, forming a waterfall and plunge pool.

questions.q: An ox-bow lake forms when:
options: The neck of a meander is cut through and the loop is cut off
questions.explain: Erosion eventually cuts through a meander neck, leaving the loop as an ox-bow lake.

questions.q: A flood hydrograph with a short lag time and high peak discharge usually indicates:
options: A gentle slow response, e.g. forested basin
A rapid flashy response, e.g. urban or impermeable basin
questions.explain: A short lag time and high peak show water reaching the river quickly, raising flood risk.

questions.q: Natural raised banks of sediment along the edges of a river channel are called:
questions.explain: Levees are raised banks built up by repeated deposition during floods.
